🇲🇽🌎 "What do we want? The best relationship with the United States. Always with respect for our sovereignty." "And that there be no political use of Mexico in the middle of the United States' electoral process." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 21, 2026 A reporter asked why, days after telling Ambassador Ronald Johnson to respect Mexican law over a training-academy deal with Querétaro's government, she called him an ally. Sheinbaum said both are true. He helped lift US sanctions that had blocked new international flights from the US to AIFA and Mexico City's airport. When Mexico disagrees, as when he went to Sinaloa to talk about corruption, it tells him directly. She also asked that the human rights of Mexicans in the US be respected and their work recognized. "That is the truth."

🇲🇽🛢️ "There is no agreement and no commitment to buy more gas." "Our objective is for that gas to be produced in Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 21, 2026 A reporter asked whether buying more US natural gas to shrink the trade deficit Trump complains about would be a step back for energy sovereignty. Sheinbaum said Washington put the idea on the table: Mexico exports more to the US than it imports, largely because of the 30-year-old trade agreement, and more gas purchases would raise Mexico's imports. Mexico's plan is to produce more of its own. In November a plant will start recovering gas now flared into the atmosphere at the Ixachi field. Gas from Cantarell is harder to use: under Fox, nitrogen was injected into the wells to push out more oil.

🇲🇽🛢️ "It stops exporting, but it no longer sells oil. Now it sells gasoline." "A vision since President López Obrador arrived: that we stop being an oil-exporting country, and that the oil we have be sold mainly for domestic consumption." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 21, 2026 La Jornada asked about Pemex's crude exports falling 45% last month as the oil went to fuel production. Mexico modernized its six refineries, built Dos Bocas and bought Deer Park. Pemex now refines 81% more oil than in 2018, and 87 of every 100 liters it sells are its own production, up from 24. About 15% of high-cost fuels are still imported. The Tula coker starts in November and Salina Cruz is building another: heavy fuel oil becomes low-sulfur gasoline and diesel, and the leftover coke will become fertilizer.

🇲🇽🔍 "They went from criticism to congratulations, and good, because the truth is they have done tireless work." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 21, 2026 A reporter noted that the chair of the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances, who once accused Mexico, now congratulates it. "They said the work done in Mexico is impressive," Sheinbaum said. The chair credits his own warning. She credits the laws changed in mid-2025 after the Teuchitlán case, an early-alert system, a deep review of the missing-persons databases, dialogue with families' search collectives, and the work of Arturo Medina, the National Search Commission, Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez and Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "The law is very clear here. Here there was Juárez, here there were liberals. Here there was a civil war over this issue that took away special privileges." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 21, 2026 Canal 14 asked about a religious association close to a PRI deputy handing awards to PAN and PRI figures inside the Chamber of Deputies, and whether churches could promote candidates in Mexico as they have elsewhere in Latin America. Sheinbaum said the Chamber should not host such events, and the law clearly limits how far all religious organizations and ministers can take part in politics. Juárez's Reform War (1858–61) separated church and state; a 1992 reform restored relations with the Vatican. "That doesn't happen in other Latin American countries because they did not live through these processes."

🇲🇽🛢️ "Today Pemex produces more energy for Mexico and generates more value inside the country." — Juan Carlos Carpio, Pemex CEO, Mañanera, Oct 21, 2026 In under two years Pemex cut its debt by more than $20 billion, to its lowest level since 2014. Its gasoline, diesel and jet fuel output is up 186% from 2018, from 350,000 to 1 million barrels a day. Gasoline and diesel sales rose 17.9% in January–September, and urea output is up 36%. Sheinbaum said the treasury once took as much as 85% from Pemex. It now pays a single 30% production duty, plus income tax, leaving more to invest. "We didn't do this to now put it back in debt up to $100 billion."
